ExpectedFailures.Renegotiate-Client: the runner takes any session ID in a renegotiation ClientHello for a resumption offer; tlsx, like crypto/tls, always sends a random 32-byte session ID and offers no session when renegotiating
ExpectedFailures.Renegotiate-Client-TLS12: as Renegotiate-Client: the random session ID of crypto/tls's ClientHello, no session offered
ExpectedFailures.Renegotiate-Client-NoExt-Allowed: tlsx renegotiates only with peers that support secure renegotiation (RFC 5746); BoringSSL also allows insecure renegotiation when renegotiation is enabled
ExpectedFailures.Renegotiate-Client-Once-2: tlsx, like crypto/tls, refuses a second renegotiation with a warning-level no_renegotiation alert (RFC 5246 7.2.2); the runner ignores warnings and expects BoringSSL's fatal alert
ExpectedFailures.ExportKeyingMaterial-Server-HalfRTT-TLS-: 0-RTT is not implemented (as in crypto/tls); Go's shim accepts -enable-early-data without acting on it, and the test runs only because tlsx's shim implements the exporter flags
